settings.name: Susan Orpen
settings.bio: Susan has been practising and teaching art in Hout Bay for over a decade. Her work spans luminous watercolour landscapes to bold acrylic abstracts.

settings.name: Kerri Sassen
settings.bio: A qualified occupational art therapist, Kerri creates a space where people explore abstraction freely — no experience needed, just an open mind.

settings.name: Zara-Leigh Farinha
settings.bio: Known for large-format abstract works in acrylic and oil, Zara-Leigh's Friday 'Permission to Play' class is joyful, free, and genuinely surprising.

settings.name: Amara Dube
settings.bio: Amara's portrait work celebrates South African faces with a richness of colour and deep sensitivity to light — each piece a quiet act of seeing.

settings.name: Liesel van der Berg
settings.bio: Working between clay and canvas, Liesel creates hand-built ceramic pieces and mixed media works that explore texture, form, and the quiet beauty of imperfection.

settings.name: Natasha Hendricks
settings.bio: Natasha layers photographic imagery with hand-pulled prints and torn paper — works that draw on Cape Town's urban landscape, memory, and overlooked moments.

settings.name: Artist 1
settings.bio: A multidisciplinary visual artist whose work explores the tension between memory and landscape. Works primarily in oil and mixed media.

settings.name: Artist 10
settings.bio: A watercolourist known for atmospheric coastal scenes and the quality of light in the Eastern Cape.

settings.name: Artist 11
settings.bio: A collage and assemblage artist who recycles found materials into densely layered narrative works.

settings.name: Artist 12
settings.bio: A young emerging artist working in acrylic on paper, drawing on Ndebele geometric traditions in a contemporary context.

settings.name: Artist 13
settings.bio: A conceptual artist whose text-based works critique commercialism, media, and post-colonial language structures.

settings.name: Artist 14
settings.bio: A landscape painter working plein air across the winelands and Drakensberg, known for intimate medium-scale oils.

settings.name: Artist 15
settings.bio: A figurative artist whose tender, intimate domestic scenes are rendered in soft graphite and coloured pencil.

settings.name: Artist 16
settings.bio: A mosaic artist whose large public commissions celebrate community heritage in Soweto and Durban.

settings.name: Artist 17
settings.bio: A linoprint artist drawing on Zulu cultural symbolism, pattern, and storytelling to create richly layered prints.

settings.name: Artist 18
settings.bio: A mixed-media artist whose work excavates personal and collective trauma through layered image and text.

settings.name: Artist 19
settings.bio: A jeweller and sculptor working at human scale, fusing precious metals with industrial off-cuts and e-waste.

settings.name: Artist 2
settings.bio: A contemporary painter known for large-scale abstract compositions. Graduated from the Michaelis School of Fine Art in Cape Town.

settings.name: Artist 20
settings.bio: A portrait photographer whose long-form documentary projects focus on youth, education, and aspiration.

settings.name: Artist 21
settings.bio: A wire sculptor whose intricate figurative works translate township life into delicate three-dimensional form.

settings.name: Artist 22
settings.bio: An abstract expressionist painter inspired by jazz, movement, and improvisation in the tradition of the Polly Street Art Centre.

settings.name: Artist 23
settings.bio: A textile artist and researcher exploring the politics of cloth, weaving, and bodily adornment in Southern Africa.

settings.name: Artist 24
settings.bio: A pen-and-ink illustrator known for intricately detailed architectural and landscape drawings of vanishing streetscapes.

settings.name: Artist 25
settings.bio: A multi-media artist whose immersive video and sound installations respond to climate, ecology, and loss.

settings.name: Artist 3
settings.bio: A sculptor and installation artist whose practice interrogates urban identity and belonging. Based in Johannesburg.

settings.name: Artist 4
settings.bio: A printmaker and draughtsperson with a deep interest in botanical forms and natural systems. Recent work focuses on the Karoo ecosystem.

settings.name: Artist 5
settings.bio: A photographer and video artist examining labour, migration, and belonging in post-apartheid South Africa.

settings.name: Artist 6
settings.bio: An interdisciplinary artist working at the intersection of textiles, performance, and archival research.

settings.name: Artist 7
settings.bio: A ceramicist whose vessels fuse functional craft with conceptual inquiry into the domestic sphere.

settings.name: Artist 8
settings.bio: A self-taught charcoal artist celebrated for emotionally charged portraiture capturing ordinary South Africans.

settings.name: Artist 9
settings.bio: A digital artist and educator whose practice spans augmented reality, generative code, and screen-based installation.

settings.name: Jacqui Sundelson
settings.bio: Jacqui is a self-taught fashion designer whose love affair with fabric began at age twelve. Over the years, she's built four distinct creative labels: Belter (her clothing label), Shloompa (bold robes and gowns), Graze & Gossip (bespoke tableware), and The House of Sunny's (textile-based interior design). She brings that same passion and precision to teaching, sharing foundational skills that open the door to a lifetime of making.

settings.name: Janice Grant
settings.bio:
I am an artist and teacher at heart, with a background in fine art, photography and graphic design. Drawing and painting are my happy place—a space where I can slow down, switch off, and just create.

I love pencil and pen, especially a good doodle where I can get lost in detail, but I also enjoy getting messy with oils and experimenting with clay. I’m happiest when I’m exploring and trying new things rather than overthinking them.

Teaching feels completely natural to me. I love sharing creativity in a relaxed, fun way where people feel free to try, play, and surprise themselves. While I don’t focus much on showing my own work, I’m passionate about helping others discover their creativity.

I’m inspired by nature, tiny details, emotions, and a lifelong love of elephants.

settings.name: Shelley Cowling
settings.bio: Shelley is a painter who celebrates the character of buildings, interiors, people, and flowers through vibrant, expressive work. She uses bold colours and loose brushstrokes to capture energy and spontaneity — the essence of her subject rather than precise detail. Her approach invites you to embrace imperfection and see beauty in the everyday.

settings.heading: Our Artists
settings.intro: Meet the artists behind The Studio — each bringing a unique voice, medium, and teaching approach to Hout Bay.
